# Meritline Tax Services

> Meritline Tax Services is an online U.S. tax compliance service for people outside the United States who own a U.S. LLC. It prepares and files Form 5472 with the pro forma Form 1120 for foreign-owned single-member LLCs, state annual reports and state tax returns, Form 7004 extensions, FBAR (FinCEN Form 114), and catch-up filings with reasonable cause statements for missed years. Clients in any country are served fully online by email and WhatsApp, with a fixed written quote before any work begins.

Last updated: 2026-11-09

## How it works

1. Request a free quote: https://meritlinetaxservices.com/contact.html#quote
2. You receive a document checklist and one fixed price in writing. A 50% deposit starts the work; the balance is due before filing.
3. Returns are prepared, reviewed with you, and filed. A foreign-owned U.S. disregarded entity cannot e-file Form 5472, so it is filed by fax or mail.
4. You receive a copy of the filed return, the fax or postal confirmation, and a free reminder before next year's deadline.

## Services and starting prices (USD)

- [Form 5472 and Pro Forma Form 1120](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/form-5472.html): from $200 per tax year; the pro forma 1120 is included
- [Form 7004 extension](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/form-5472.html): $100 per tax year
- [State annual reports](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/state-filings.html): $100 plus the state fee (Wyoming, Delaware, Florida and other states; New Mexico LLCs have no annual report)
- [State tax returns](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/state-filings.html): from $100 per state
- [Late filings and multi-year catch-up](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/late-filings.html): prior-year return from $200; multi-year catch-up quoted by the number of years missed
- [Reasonable cause statement](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/late-filings.html): from $250
- [IRS notice review](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/late-filings.html): from $150
- FBAR (FinCEN Form 114): from $150 per year
- [Other business returns](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/services.html): Form 1120 (C corporation) from $300; Form 1065 with Schedule K-1 from $300
- [Individual returns](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/services.html): Form 1040 from $150
- [LLC formation](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/services.html): from $200 plus state fee; LLC formation with EIN $250 plus state fee; EIN assistance $75
- [Bookkeeping](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/services.html): from $125 per month
- [Consultations](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/services.html#consultations): free 20-minute introductory call; paid consultations from $30
- [Full pricing](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/pricing.html)

State fees, government fees and any tax owed are paid separately.

## Core guides

- [Form 5472 Instructions Explained: The Complete Guide for Foreign Owners of U.S. LLCs](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/blog/form-5472-explained.html): who must file, reportable transactions, what each part asks, filing by fax, penalties, common mistakes
- [Form 5472 Example: A Completed Sample for a Foreign-Owned Single-Member LLC](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/blog/form-5472-example-filled-out.html): Form 5472 and the pro forma Form 1120 filled in for a fictional LLC, line by line, with a free PDF
- [Can I File Form 5472 Myself? A Practical Guide for Foreign LLC Owners](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/blog/can-i-file-form-5472-myself.html): honest self-check, DIY steps, common mistakes, and a DIY review option
- [Foreign-Owned LLC Taxes: The Complete Guide for Non-U.S. Owners](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/blog/foreign-owned-llc-taxes.html): how the IRS treats a foreign-owned single-member LLC, Form 5472, when U.S. income tax applies, other forms, state obligations, and a yearly calendar
- [How to Get an EIN Without an SSN: A Guide for Foreign LLC Owners](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/blog/how-to-get-ein-without-ssn.html): how a foreign owner applies for an LLC's EIN by phone, fax, or mail, and completes Form SS-4 (lines 7b and 9a) before the first Form 5472
- [Form 5472 With No Income: Do You Still Need to File?](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/blog/form-5472-no-income.html): why a foreign-owned LLC with no income usually still files, which transactions count, and when a dormant year has no filing
- [Form 5472 Deadline 2026 and 2027: IRS Due Dates for Foreign-Owned LLCs](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/blog/form-5472-deadline-2026-2027.html): the 2026 tax year return is due April 15, 2027, or October 15, 2027 with Form 7004
- [Form 5472 Filing Extension: How to File Form 7004 for a Foreign-Owned U.S. LLC](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/blog/form-5472-extension-form-7004.html): foreign-owned LLCs fax Form 7004 to 855-887-7737 or mail it to the dedicated Ogden, Utah address
- [Form 5472 Late Filing Penalty Abatement: Reasonable Cause Letter and Relief Steps](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/blog/form-5472-late-filing-penalty-abatement.html): the $25,000 penalty, reasonable cause, first-time abatement limits, appeals
- [Missed the October 15 Form 5472 Deadline? What Foreign-Owned LLCs Should Do Now](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/blog/missed-october-15-form-5472-deadline.html)
- [Form 5472 Tax Year: Calendar Years, Fiscal Years, and Your First Short Year](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/blog/form-5472-tax-year-due-dates.html): calendar year, fiscal year, and the first short year
- [Do U.S. Owners Need Form 5472? Who Files and Who Does Not](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/blog/form-5472-us-owners-and-corporations.html)
- [Form 1120 vs. Form 1065: Which Tax Return Does Your U.S. Business File?](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/blog/form-1120-vs-form-1065.html)
- [Tax Deadlines 2027: When Are U.S. Taxes Due? A Calendar for Businesses and Individuals](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/blog/us-tax-deadlines-2027.html)
- [U.S. LLC Tax Glossary for Foreign Owners: 52 Terms Explained in Plain English](https://meritlinetaxservices.com/blog/us-llc-tax-glossary.html): plain-English definitions of 52 terms, from Form 5472 and disregarded entity to ECI, FBAR, and franchise tax
